[1/2] Web-based Start button: localhost-only stdlib HTTP launcher with a branded page, token-protected /start, fixed play/demo commands, Windows new-console spawn, Studio served at /studio/ with traversal guards, port validation and error triads. [2/2] End-to-end verification in Edge (Start spawned a real game process; Studio served 8 models), HTTP/unit/CLI tests, README/ADR-022, Phase 4.

impact_assessment.why: The user asked for a web-based start button; browsers cannot spawn local processes directly, and a full in-browser game server is a much larger change. A localhost launcher starts the real game honestly and links the Studio.
impact_assessment.benefits: One local page covers Start Game, Watch Demo and the browser Studio; no Python dependency; the game still runs natively with full input performance.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: new --serve/--open flags and localhost HTTP surface; security: arbitrary process spawn if unguarded; dependency: none; concurrency: ThreadingHTTPServer can field parallel /start calls, so repeated clicks can open multiple games though only fixed commands are possible; state: no persisted launcher state; platform: automatic terminal launch is Windows-only.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Localhost bind, random per-process token on every launch, fixed command list, no request-supplied paths/args, traversal-guarded Studio file serving, port validation, HTTP/unit tests and a real Edge click that spawned and then stopped the game process.

checkpoints.description: Shipped launcher.py: ThreadingHTTPServer on 127.0.0.1 with a branded START GAME/WATCH DEMO page, random token required on POST /start, fixed argv (never request-supplied), Windows CREATE_NEW_CONSOLE launch, Studio served from .inspect under /studio/ with flat-name traversal guards, health and favicon endpoints, and --serve/--open/port validation in the CLI. End-to-end verified in Edge: the page rendered, the Start click returned success and spawned real PID 20944 (then stopped), and /studio/ served the Studio with all 8 models. The hygiene gate flagged the intentional detached Popen, webbrowser.open and silent Ctrl+C; fixed with an explicit hygiene rationale, open_new_tab, and a stop message.

[1/2] True one-click start: --autostart (with --serve) opens the launcher at ?autostart=1; the page strips the query, sets a one-shot session guard and launches the game automatically. Add PLAY_WEB.bat (Windows double-click) and play_web.sh, plus idempotent serve (health check reopens the page instead of failing). [2/2] Add a 2-second server-side duplicate-launch guard, HTTP/unit/CLI tests, README/ADR-023, and Phase 4.

impact_assessment.why: The web Start button still needed a terminal command first; the user asked for one-click start, and launching a second server on the same port failed instead of reopening the page.
impact_assessment.benefits: Double-clicking PLAY_WEB.bat starts the launcher, opens the browser and starts the real native game with no further click; reloads and double-clicks cannot spawn duplicate games; a second launch just reopens the page.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: --autostart flag, autostart query and one-click launcher files; security: autostart only with the per-process token, localhost bind and fixed commands; dependency: none; concurrency: ThreadingHTTPServer plus a lock and a 2 s same-mode coalescing window; state: only client sessionStorage; platform: automatic terminal launch remains Windows-only, POSIX gets the page and exact command.
impact_assessment.mitigation: HTTP tests for page/token/duplicate coalescing/health, unit tests for URL/token/traversal, CLI tests for autostart/port/open validation, launcher-file tests, and a real Edge autostart run (status success, query stripped, session flag set).

checkpoints.description: Shipped one-click start: --autostart (requires --serve) opens the launcher at /?autostart=1; the page strips the query, sets sessionStorage guard, and POSTs the token-protected play request. serve() health-checks the port and, if a launcher already owns it, only reopens the browser. Added a 2 s same-mode duplicate-launch lock so double-clicks/reloads cannot spawn two games. Added PLAY_WEB.bat (Windows double-click: serve + browser + autostart) and play_web.sh, plus README tree and ADR-023. Verified in Edge: /?autostart=1 returned 'Game launched in a new console window', history lost the query, and the one-shot flag was set; earlier Start-path verification had already spawned a real game process. HTTP tests cover token rejection, duplicate coalescing, health; unit/CLI tests cover URL helpers, traversal, autostart/port/open validation and launcher files.

[1/3] Browser edition on the same engine: WebGame + WebTerm, 20 fps session thread, chars/colour frames, canvas client with keyboard/mouse, token-protected input, lazy 9 s forge, idle pause, separate web save. [2/3] Launcher integration: /play, /api/frame, /api/state, /api/input, PLAY IN BROWSER, --open-play; PLAY_WEB.bat/play_web.sh open the browser game directly while PLAY.bat/terminal stays unchanged. [3/3] Verify live in Edge (canvas, movement, menus, save/continue), add unit/HTTP tests, README/ADR-024, Phase 4.

impact_assessment.why: The user clarified they wanted the game itself in both the browser and the current terminal; a launcher/Studio alone did not satisfy that.
impact_assessment.benefits: The browser runs the real Python game with no duplicated logic and no new dependency; the terminal build remains the canonical experience, and both share worlds, HUD, weather and saves per slot.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: new /play, /api/frame, /api/state and /api/input endpoints plus --open-play; security: /api/input is token-protected and the server binds localhost, while frame/state reads are local-only and unauthenticated; dependency: none; concurrency: a 20 fps session thread guarded by an RLock, one shared session across tabs; state: web saves go to saves/aldervale_web.json and the terminal save is untouched; resource: the session pauses after 20 s without polling.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Live Playwright verification of canvas size/render time/movement/menus/save/continue, HTTP tests for frame/state/input/auth, unit tests for WebTerm and frame encoding, 162 tests and 4/4 gates, separate save slot and idle pause.

impact_assessment.risks: contract: none, docs and launcher scripts only; dependency: none; concurrency: none; state: none
impact_assessment.mitigation: Failing-first tests for launcher detection and README completeness, 164 tests, 4/4 gates

[1/2] Deliver the accumulated web edition, launcher, weather and model work; fix the browser session diverging from the terminal loop

impact_assessment.why: Review of everything uncommitted since the last push found the browser session ran its own copy of the frame step: it advanced the world while menus were open, never entered the death state (so no death screen and no respawn), never armed the victory overlay, and let mouse events queue without bound. The one-click browser launcher also lacked the documented --version fast path PLAY.bat has.
impact_assessment.benefits: The browser build now pauses, dies and wins exactly like the terminal; one shared step removes the duplication that caused the drift; the launcher behaves like PLAY.bat.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: Game.tick is a new shared entry point; dependency: none; concurrency: the 20 fps session thread calls tick under its RLock; state: no save format change; behaviour: terminal loop must stay identical
impact_assessment.mitigation: Direct tests for Game.tick (menu freeze, death, victory clock) and WebGame.step delegation, bounded mouse queue, live Edge run of menu/death/respawn/victory, 170 tests and 4/4 gates
